about.title: Auburn Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products cause injuries far beyond the crash reports that dominate corridors like Grass Valley Highway, I-80, and Auburn Folsom Road. A faulty vehicle part, a malfunctioning tool at a job site near Rt 49, or a household appliance that fails without warning can leave someone in Auburn with serious, lasting harm. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a strict liability claim, meaning the focus is on whether the product itself was defective — not on proving the manufacturer was careless. LawProactive helps Auburn residents connect, free of charge, with an independent attorney who understands how to evaluate a defective product claim, identify which companies in the chain of distribution may share responsibility, and explain what evidence matters most. We never charge for this connection, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless a recovery is made. Preserving the product exactly as it was at the time of injury is one of the most important steps you can take.

whyChoose.title: Why Auburn Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Means a Different Legal Path
items.desc: California generally lets injured people focus on whether the product was defective, not on proving the manufacturer was negligent. That can simplify what you need to show to move a claim forward.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers can potentially be held liable under California product liability law. An attorney can help sort out who was actually involved in getting that product into your hands.

items.title: Preserving Evidence Matters Early On
items.desc: Because the product itself is often the central piece of evidence in a defect claim, keeping it unaltered and unrepaired can make a real difference. We can help you get guidance on this quickly.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often proceed under strict liability, which generally means you need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This is different from many other injury claims that require proving negligence.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, without repairing or discarding it. It's often the most important piece of evidence in these cases, so an attorney will likely want to examine it directly.

items.question: Is this only for injuries connected to car crashes on roads like Grass Valley Highway or Auburn Folsom Road?
items.answer: No. While Auburn sees a notable number of injury collisions each year on corridors like these, product liability claims cover any defective product — from vehicle components to household items to job-site equipment. If a product malfunctioned and caused you harm anywhere in Placer County, it may be worth having a claim reviewed.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
